# Overarch Template Instructions
These instructions apply to the Comb templates and template libraries under
`/templates`, which generate artifacts (reports, docs, diagrams, code) from an
Overarch model. See [doc/topics/templates.md](/doc/topics/templates.md) for
the full reference. For Comb syntax itself, see `cmb.instructions.md`.

## Available bindings
Every `.cmb` template is evaluated with these symbols bound, no `require` needed:
* `e` - the selected element or view being rendered (for `:per-element true`, a single node/view/relation; otherwise the whole selected collection)
* `model` - the full model, for navigation via `m/*` functions
* `view` - the current view, when rendering in a view context
* `ctx` - the generation context map from the generation config (e.g. `(:title ctx)`, `(:template ctx)`, plus any custom namespaced keys added there)
* `protected-areas` - map of protected-area marker name -> preserved content, for round-tripping manual edits (see below)

## Available namespace aliases
No `require` needed for these; use directly via alias:
* `str` -> `clojure.string` (e.g. `str/join`, `str/capitalize`)
* `set` -> `clojure.set`
* `sstr` -> `org.soulspace.clj.string`
* `m` -> model API (`org.soulspace.overarch.adapter.template.model-api`) - query/navigate the model, e.g. `m/resolve-element`, `m/referring-nodes`, `m/referred-nodes`, `m/children`, `m/element-type`
* `v` -> view API (`org.soulspace.overarch.adapter.template.view-api`) - query/navigate views, e.g. `v/view-elements`, `v/title`

Only require namespaces that are not already available as aliases above.

## Template libraries (`templates/lib`)
Reusable helper functions live under `templates/lib` and are pulled in with `(require '[lib.x :as x])` at the top of a template:
* `lib.text` (as `t`) - text helpers: `single-line`, `multi-lines`, `tokenize-string`, `escape-html`, `wrap-string`
* `lib.markdown` (as `md`) - Markdown link/table generators: `relative-element-link`, `relative-diagram-link`, `relative-view-link`, `node-description-table`, `relation-description-table`, `technical-relation-description-table`
* `lib.graphviz`, `lib.mermaid`, `lib.plantuml` (and `lib.plantuml.uml`/`wbs`/`c4`) - diagram-syntax generators for the respective view templates

When a template needs logic beyond simple lookups, prefer adding a function to the matching `lib` namespace over inlining large `<% ... %>` blocks, so the logic is reusable across templates. Keep `lib/*.clj` functions pure and free of side effects - they only receive data (elements, models, strings) and return values or strings for the template to emit.

## Template conventions used in this repo
* Start each template with a comment block naming its purpose and, if relevant, the generation-config expectations it relies on, e.g.:
  ```
  <%
  ;;;;
  ;;;; Markdown Documentation Template for a Model Node
  ;;;;
  ;;;; config:
  ;;;;  :per-element true
  ;;;;  :id-as-name  true
  ;;;;
  (require '[lib.text :as t])
  (require '[lib.markdown :as md])
  %>
  ```
* Filter model nodes/relations by `:el` with `(filter #(= :system (:el %)) ...)`, wrap in `(seq ...)` and use `when-let` so a section is only emitted if there is content.
* Sort collections with `sort-by :name` before rendering tables/lists.
* Wrap a template body in a top-level `(let [...] ... )` when several derived values (referring/referred nodes, parent, children, etc. via `m/*`) are reused across sections; close the `let` right before the final "generated by" footer.
* End generated Markdown artifacts with:
  ```
  (generated by [Overarch](https://github.com/soulspace-org/overarch) with template <%= (:template ctx) %>)
  ```
* Match the filename pattern `<basename>.<target-extension>.cmb` (e.g. `node.md.cmb`, `view.dot.cmb`, `avro.avsc.cmb`) so the target artifact type is clear from the template name; keep templates grouped by purpose under `templates/docs`, `templates/reports`, `templates/views`, `templates/arc42`, `templates/exports`.

## Protected areas
* Mark manually-edited regions with matching begin/end comments using the configured marker (default `PA`), e.g. `// PA-BEGIN(name)` / `// PA-END(name)`, and re-emit the preserved content between them with `(:name protected-areas)`.
* Only add protected areas where a human is expected to fill in logic or content  the model cannot express (e.g. method bodies); don't add them speculatively.

## Generation config awareness
* Templates are applied per the generation config (see `templates/gencfg.edn` and [doc/topics/templates.md](/doc/topics/templates.md)); when adding a new template, also add or update its generation-context entry (`:selection`/`:view-selection`, `:template`, `:per-element`, `:extension`, etc.).
* Custom (namespaced) keys added to a generation-context map are available via `ctx` in the template - use this instead of hardcoding values that a generation config might want to vary.
